extracted.intended_audience: IP office staff, policymakers, researchers, and practitioners tracking trademark statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Indicators, definitions and table/figure titles used in WIPO's World Intellectual Property Indicators for trademarks (applications, registrations, registrations in force, class counts, procedural and sector breakdowns) covering 2010–2024 and 2024 cross-sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active trademark registrations / Trademark registrations in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of active trademark registrations across IP offices (e.g., 'an estimated 93.2 million active trademark registrations across 155 IP offices globally') and growth rate (e.g., 'grew 6.1% globally in 2024').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO note: 'World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 170 IP offices.' Figures may include regional office effects (see notes on Paris route and Madrid System). Use for cross‑office comparisons and time trends (Figure B34, B35, B36).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trend in trademark applications (absolute counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual counts of trademark applications filed worldwide for each application year (time series 2010–2024) and associated growth rates (percentage changes year-on-year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Totals include applications filed directly at national/regional offices (Paris route) and designations received via the Madrid System where applicable. Source: WIPO Statistics Database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark application class count
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of Nice classes specified in trademark applications (application class count) reported by year and office (Figures B2, B5, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class count = number of classes specified in an application/registration. Used to adjust for multi‑class filings; figures may differ from single-application counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registration class count
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of Nice classes specified in trademark registrations (registration class count) reported by year and office (Figure B5, B15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration class counts reflect classes in issued registrations. Differences between single-class and multi-class systems across offices are not adjusted for unless explicitly stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident and non-resident trademark application/registration class counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of application or registration class counts into resident and non-resident shares (Figures B3, B6 and many regional/office tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resident/non-resident status determined by applicant's residence. Useful for assessing international filing activity and domestic filing strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident share (%) / Resident share (%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of application or registration class counts attributable to non-resident (or resident) filers at an office or origin (many figures show 'Non-resident share (%)' and 'Resident share (%)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare reliance on domestic vs foreign filing; shown alongside absolute counts and growth rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution of resident and non-resident application class counts to total growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Decomposition of total growth (or decline) in application class counts into contributions made by resident and non-resident filings (Figures B10, B12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how much of year-on-year growth is driven by resident vs non-resident activity; helpful for diagnosing sources of growth/decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark applications/registrations by office and by origin (top 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and class counts for the top offices and top origins (Figures B9, B15, B17, B20) with resident vs non-resident splits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures/tables present absolute and (where applicable) equivalent counts for regional offices. Use to identify major filing/registration centers and origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application / Registration time trends for top offices (long-run series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term time-series of application or registration counts for top offices (e.g., 1883–2024 trends for top five offices, Figures B8, B14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for historical context; note that counting rules and filing systems (single vs multi-class) can affect comparability over long spans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registrations in force as percentage of registrations recorded between 2000 and 2024
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of registrations from a given year (or range) that remain in force in 2024 (Figure B36: e.g., 'Almost one-quarter (24.5%) of the trademarks registered in 2000 remained in force in 2024').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess longevity/retention of marks. Based on subset of offices where registration-year distribution is available; caution on coverage (23.8 million registrations in force at 86 offices mentioned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of trademarks in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Average age (in years) of trademarks currently in force at selected offices (Figure B37).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of how long marks are typically maintained; interpret together with renewals rules and national practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective and certification trademark applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of collective trademark applications and certification trademark applications by office (Figures B32, B33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct legal forms of marks; reported separately to capture sector-specific filing patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of trademark applications by Nice class (top classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Share (%) distribution of non-resident trademark applications across Nice classes (Figure B23: ranked classes and shares).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Class descriptions abbreviated in figure; refer to Nice Classification for full descriptions. Figures are based on non-resident filing data from a subset of offices (e.g., 141 IP offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident trademark applications: goods vs services classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Share split between goods classes and services classes in the Nice Classification (e.g., '72.0% Goods classes / 28.0% Services classes') (Figure B24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on 45-class Nice Classification where first 34 classes = goods, remaining 11 = services. Coverage limited to reporting offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident trademark applications by industry sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of non-resident applications across industry sectors derived from Nice class groups, with sector shares and absolute class counts (Figure B25).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sector groupings and mappings from Nice classes are defined in the annex; some sector names abbreviated. Based on non-resident filing data from selected offices (e.g., 141 IP offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top sectors by office / top sectors by origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Top three industry sectors for top offices and top origins (Figures B26, B28) showing sector shares at office/origin level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to profile sectoral specialization across offices/origins. See annex for class-to-sector mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark application class count abroad: absolute vs equivalent counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of classes filed abroad by origin, with both absolute counts (regional office filings counted once) and equivalent counts (regional filings treated as multiple national filings) and an 'equivalent/absolute count ratio' (Figure B19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute count: regional filings counted once; Equivalent count: regional filings expanded to member states. Choose metric appropriate for the analysis; the ratio indicates the regional-office effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flows of non-resident trademark application class counts between origins and offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Matrix/flow figures showing non-resident filing flows from selected top origins to destination offices (Figure B21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Origin data are based on absolute counts. Useful for mapping international filing patterns; interpret with awareness of regional-office counting conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark application class count per USD 100 billion GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident trademark application class count normalized per USD 100 billion GDP for selected origins (Figure B30).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalizes filing intensity by economic size; check currency/year of GDP used and country coverage when comparing across origins or years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident trademark application class count per million population
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident trademark application class count normalized per million population for selected origins (Figure B31).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalizes by population to compare filing intensity; ensure consistent population data vintage when comparing years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark office procedural data: examination outcomes, pendency, examiners, duration, oppositions, appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural indicators reported by office: distribution of trademark examination outcomes, potentially pending trademark applications, number of trademark examiners, duration of trademark examination, third‑party oppositions, appeals against decisions (Figures B38–B43; table B46).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operational metrics measure office workload and performance. Definitions and coverage vary by office; refer to table B46 and notes for office-specific methodology and caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth rate (%) and Average growth (%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Year-on-year percentage growth rates for counts (applications, class counts, registrations) and multi-year average growth percentages shown alongside absolute counts in many figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Growth rates provide trend context; examine both absolute and percentage changes, and note the base year and office coverage for comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes on coverage and definitions (Paris route, Madrid System, office coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifying notes used repeatedly: 'World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 170 IP offices. Each total includes the number of applications filed directly at national or regional offices (the Paris route), as well as the number of designations received by offices via the Madrid System (where applicable).' Also: definitions of class count, resident/non-resident, absolute vs equivalent counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitional notes are essential to correctly interpret all above metrics. Always apply the stated coverage and counting rules when comparing figures across offices or over time.
